description: Committee recommends amending taxi bylaw for payment and van rates.
Committee requests report on taxi driver safety options.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Dubois questioned van rate calculation discrepancy, $30,000 vs $14,000 capital cost.
Taxi drivers and brokerage companies are directly affected by proposed bylaw changes.
Administration prefers broker-owned payment machines; drivers prefer owning their own.
Administration could not immediately provide specific van trip numbers to recoup capital costs.
Taxi drivers expressed concerns about payment delays and unfair van rates.
Councillor Dubois could not support van rate due to lack of higher operating cost accounting.
Administration is developing a deposit-based payment system for taxi industry.

speakers.name: Malik Draz
speakers.organization: Taxi Drivers and Franchise Owners Association
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Amendments to Vehicles for Hire Bylaw
said: Agreed with most proposed bylaw amendments (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7).
Opposed amendment 5 on point-of-sale machines due to delayed driver payments.
Concerned new van rates will decrease driver earnings and are unfair.

speakers.name: Adnan Ahmad
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Amendments to The Vehicles for Hire Bylaw
said: Van rates should apply for less than five people if customer has luggage or disability.
Airport flat rates are clear for sedans, but van rates are not mentioned.
Drivers should offer meter or airport flat rate options for vans.

description: Approves new criteria for prioritizing sidewalk and cycling path projects.

chips.text: Approved
9 for, 0 against

Walking Saskatoon expressed concerns about criteria implementation and consultation.
New sidewalk criteria specifically include an 'equity part' for prioritization.
